text:
Alex W.: heads up — after yesterday's KMS policy tweak the onprem privctl agent started failing to fetch keys for a subset of dedicated tenants. saw ~20% request errors this morning.
Maya S.: ugh. symptoms? 403s from KMS, or agent-level errors?
Alex W.: 403 from KMS with `AccessDenied`; agent logs show `key access denied: principal not in kms:Grant` followed by retries.
Sam R.: can you paste the policy diff you applied? maybe a condition got tightened.
Alex W.: pasted below
```json
- "Statement": [{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":"*","Action":"kms:Decrypt","Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/old-key"}]
+ "Statement": [{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/privctl"},"Action":"kms:Decrypt","Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/new-key","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"kms:CallerAccount":"111222333"}}}]
```
Jordan P.: that Condition looks fine but I recall we also rolled a roles/privctl@onprem binding change yesterday — possible mismatch between the IAM role in the policy and the ephemeral identities that privctl uses.
Lee T.: is there any VPC allowlist or tenant mapping that could cause the principal to be different? dedicated/private deployments have per-tenant service accounts, right?
Alex W.: yes — privctl on-prem uses short-lived service identities that get exchanged to an IAM role via the control plane. if the control plane cached the old mapping (tenant -> iam role) you can end up calling KMS with an unexpected principal.
Maya S.: that sounds like a race between the RBAC refactor and the KMS policy rollout. did we invalidate the control plane's allowlist cache when the role bindings changed?
Alex W.: apparently not. I grepped the controlplane logs: `skip cache invalidation for allowlist update` from 03:12 UTC.
Sam R.: can we quickly mitigate by temporarily adding a permissive statement for the prev role set? e.g. allow both `role/privctl` and the old `role/privctl-temp` until we rotate caches.
Jordan P.: yes, but prefer minimal blast radius: add `kms:Decrypt` for the specific tenant key ARNs used by the affected tenants. ops can patch policy now.
Lee T.: also plan: (1) flush controlplane allowlist cache, (2) issue a coordinated short window to rotate the mapping, (3) watch audit logs for `kms:Decrypt` denies.
operations-bot: runbook triggered — flushing allowlist cache for cluster-onprem-2 now. job id: r-93a4
Alex W.: thanks. i'll coordinate with infra to patch KMS policy. also let's collect audit logs for the 03:00-04:00 window.
Maya S.: FYI, audit logs show 32 denied Decrypts from `tenant-42` and 4 from `tenant-77`.
Sam R.: ok i'll open a short-lived policy PR and tag @jordan for review. will leave an explicit expiry comment (30m) so we don't forget to revert.
Jordan P.: approved the hotfix PR. once ops confirms cache flush, i'll remove the temporary statement and we can push a clean role-binding rollout with cache invalidation.
Lee T.: action items: Alex apply policy hotfix, ops confirm cache flush, Jordan validate role mapping and schedule proper rollout with cache invalidation hook. put postmortem if we see >0 customer impact.
Alex W.: noted. i'll also add a test to the controlplane CI that simulates role-binding change + allowlist update to ensure cache invalidation is exercised.
Maya S.: thanks — and please ping #oncall if any tenants see degraded decrypts after revert.
Sam R.: :thumbsup:
